work.text: Drug candidates on paper. Each epoch a miner submits one string holding 20 small molecules, written as reaction plus building blocks, and one nanobody sequence, both aimed at the target proteins named for that epoch. The string is timelock-encrypted, uploaded to the miner's public GitHub repository, and a pointer is committed on chain. Nothing is synthesized; what is paid for is a predicted binder.
work.quote: Submission: One string molecules|sequences, encrypted and uploaded; chain stores the GitHub path.

scoring.text: Validators decrypt every entry after the epoch closes and reject any that fails format, the epoch's allowed reaction, uniqueness per target, or a similarity ceiling against past submissions. Molecules are scored by Boltz-2, a structure-prediction model, on predicted binding affinity to the target, normalized by heavy-atom count; higher wins. Nanobodies are ranked by BoltzGen on confidence, physical interaction and developability; lowest rank sum wins.

split.text: Winner takes all, twice over: 60 percent of the miner weight to the best molecule entry, 40 percent to the best nanobody, ties to the earliest committed block. A type with no valid winner sends its share to UID 0. At this commit the payout override is on: the validator sets all weight on UID 42 and posts each winner's share to an emission-transfer API that pays off chain.
split.disagrees: docs/MINER.md and the site's nova page say the winner per type receives the incentive; the code at the pinned commit, with config/config.yaml payout.enabled true and override_uid 42, puts all on-chain weight on UID 42 and pays winners through emission-transfer-api.metanova-labs.ai (neurons/validator/payouts.py).

judges.text: Five validators were active on the 2026-09-09 chain snapshot. Commit-reveal is on. A validator re-runs the whole judgment itself: it decrypts every entry, runs Boltz-2 and BoltzGen on two 48 GB GPUs, and picks the winners. Nothing is sampled. A team-issued VALIDATOR_API_KEY turns on score sharing and monitoring with Metanova's servers. The bonds moving average is set to 1.
judges.quote: commit_reveal_weights_enabled True, weights_rate_limit 100, bonds_moving_avg 1; chain-2026-09-09.json active_validators 5

cadence.text: Emission settles every 360 blocks, about 72 minutes. The competition epoch in the code is 361 blocks, one block longer, so the two drift against each other. Commitments in the last 10 blocks of an epoch are ignored. The epoch's target and allowed reaction are derived from its start block hash. A new registration is immune from deregistration for 5,000 blocks, about 16 hours.
cadence.quote: tempo 360, immunity_period 5000; MINER.md: Competitions last for 361 blocks; config.yaml no_submission_blocks: 10

buyer.text: No paying customer is named and there is no price. The partnerships page offers screening as a service, co-development and custom competitions to biotech and pharmaceutical organizations, and names two partners: OnePot.AI, a robotic synthesis lab that makes the hits, and Yalotein, for whom the nanobody track was built. The miner's income is the epoch bounty.
buyer.quote: We are open to partnering with biotech, pharmaceutical, and research organizations to collaborate beyond traditional service agreements.

exploits.text: Resubmitting past winners or near-copies: a molecule with Tanimoto similarity of 0.5 or more to any prior submission for the target invalidates the whole entry; duplicates per target are rejected; the 20 molecules must clear a fingerprint entropy floor of 0.25; nanobodies within 0.95 of the target's top 50 are rejected. Timelock encryption stops copying inside an epoch. The miner guide says the unmodified baseline earns nothing.
exploits.quote: max_similarity_to_historical: 0.5 # maximum similarity to historical submissions to be considered valid
